needs.question: Should I apply to the Getting Ready or the Working with/in/for Community stream of the EDI fund?

needs.yorkAnswer: Getting Ready builds team EDI readiness and capacity; the Community stream supports partnerships with underrepresented communities and accessible co-creation.

needs.question: What do I need to write in an EDI Member-Initiated Fund application, and what are the word limits?
needs.statement: I need to know the required sections and limits so that my application is complete.
needs.yorkAnswer: Initiative description (350 words), impacts (250), previous community experience (100), Getting Ready reflection (100), fund use (125), plus a line-by-line budget.

evidence.quote: Description of the Initiative (350 words max)
evidence.gist: Initiative description (350 words), impacts (250), previous community experience (100), Getting Ready reflection (100), fund use (125) plus line-by-line budget.

needs.question: How are EDI Member-Initiated Fund applications scored?
needs.statement: I need to know the scoring weights so that I focus my application effort where it counts.
needs.yorkAnswer: Description 50%, impacts 25%, previous experience 15%, budget 10%; over 70% is fundable; consensus vote decides.

evidence.quote: Applications scoring over 70% will be deemed fundable and discussed during an EDI Committee meeting.
evidence.gist: Description 50%, impacts 25%, previous experience 15%, budget 10%; over 70% is fundable; consensus vote decides.

needs.question: When will I hear back about my EDI Member-Initiated Fund application?
needs.statement: I need to know the decision timeline so that I can plan my initiative.
needs.yorkAnswer: Submitted via MachForm in January, adjudicated January/February, results emailed in February (tentative).

evidence.quote: Final results will be sent out via email in February.
evidence.gist: Submitted via MachForm in January, adjudicated January/February, results emailed in February (tentative).

needs.question: What does co-creation mean in Connected Minds research?
needs.statement: I need the definition of co-creation so that my project meets the expectation.
needs.yorkAnswer: Working with affected people, communities and sectors (and across disciplines) to jointly define problems, design/test ideas and evaluate outcomes.

evidence.quote: Co-creation is a collaborative approach to research wherein researchers work directly with the people, communities, and sectors affected by an issue
evidence.gist: Researchers work with affected people, communities and sectors to jointly define problems, design and test ideas, and evaluate outcomes; can also be across disciplines.

evidence.quote: Co-creation is a collaborative and transformative research approach wherein researchers work directly with the people
evidence.gist: Collaborative approach working with affected people, communities and sectors to jointly define problems, design/test ideas and evaluate outcomes.

needs.question: What is the difference between epistemic and application-oriented co-creation?
needs.statement: I need to distinguish the two types so that I describe my project correctly.
needs.yorkAnswer: Epistemic combines disciplines/knowledge systems to shape problems and priorities; application-oriented has researchers, developers and end users iteratively develop and test innovations.

evidence.quote: it must operate along two complementary dimensions: epistemic (formerly “horizontal”) and application-oriented (formerly “vertical”) co-creation
evidence.gist: Epistemic (formerly horizontal) shapes questions and priorities; application-oriented (formerly vertical) refines prototypes and interventions; both span the full lifecycle.

evidence.quote: Epistemic Co-Creation involves bringing together different academic disciplines, policy and legal expertise, art, and non-academic knowledge systems
evidence.gist: Epistemic: combining disciplines and knowledge systems to define problems; application-oriented: researchers, developers and end users iteratively develop and test innovations.

needs.question: Which type of co-creation must my Connected Minds project include?
needs.statement: I need to know the mandatory co-creation types so that my application is eligible.
needs.yorkAnswer: All projects must include epistemic co-creation; projects translating research to application must also include application-oriented collaboration with developers and end users.

evidence.quote: All projects must include epistemic co-creation (collaboration across disciplinary and epistemic domains).
evidence.gist: Yes; all projects must include epistemic co-creation across disciplinary and epistemic domains.

evidence.quote: Projects involving translation of research to application must also include applicaton co-creation
evidence.gist: Projects translating research to application must include iterative collaboration among researchers, developers and end users.
